theory.intro: Two straight lines meet at a single **point of intersection**, unless they are parallel. The coordinates of that point are the one pair of $x$ and $y$ values that satisfy **both** equations at the same time, so reading the crossing point off an accurate graph solves the pair simultaneously.
facts: Graph both lines on the same axes, then read the coordinates of the point where they cross.
Write the solution as an ordered pair $(x,y)$, or as $x=\ldots$, $y=\ldots$; the crossing point gives both values at once.
The point of intersection lies on both lines, so its coordinates make **both** equations true.
Parallel lines have equal gradients and never cross, so the pair has **no solution**.
Two equations describing the **same** line cross at every point, so the pair has **infinitely many solutions**.
steps: Locate the point where the two lines cross.

There are infinitely many simultaneous solutions.
